title: How v0 aims to create 100 million builders: Rauch on AI, taste and exposure hours
summary: Guillermo Rauch explains why v0 exists (growing the pool of product builders from ~20M JavaScript developers to 100M), how specialist "translation tasks" are being absorbed by AI, and how to build taste through exposure hours. He also covers tight in-product feedback loops, escape hatches, and how Vercel's teams ship with AI.

principles.text: Size your market by who aspires to build, not who can code: 100M product builders vs ~20M JS developers.
principles.quote: how many product builders or people with aspirations of building products exist my back of the napkin like minimum calculation is 100 million

principles.text: Bet on open source early: your tools end up in model training data, so AI is natively good at your stack.
principles.quote: our tools are already in the training data of the internet and so that long-term bet and vision and open source really paid off

principles.text: Tasks that are really translation (design to code) get automated; knowing how things work remains valuable for steering the model.
principles.quote: Knowing those tokens is going to be very important for you because you're going to be able to influence the model and make it follow your intention a lot better.

principles.text: Taste is a learnable skill: quantify and increase the hours you spend watching people use products.
principles.quote: Try to quantify how much time you expose yourself to watching how people use your products.

principles.text: Build many in-product feedback channels from day one; AI products create a constant stream that improves each iteration.
principles.quote: create a lot of opportunities for people to give you feedback inside the product.

principles.text: Great products need creative restraint: every feature is like adopting a puppy, so say no far more than yes.
principles.quote: the best product builders will say nine nos for every yes because when you say yes is like adopting a puppy.
